title: SoundGraph Patch
description: The canonical, portable representation of a SoundGraph patch. This document is the product; editors, runtimes and hardware targets are consumers of it. Anything a frontend needs in order to reproduce a patch must round-trip through this format.

schema_version.description: Incremented only for breaking changes. A runtime must refuse a patch whose schema_version it does not implement. Version 2 adds modules; a document without modules stays version 1.

modules.description: Module definitions, by name. Present only in version 2 documents.

arrangement.description: Optional presentation hints. Never affects what a patch sounds like, and a runtime that only wants to make sound should ignore this whole object. Node positions and cable waypoints stay on the elements they describe; this is for hints about a whole view, which have nothing to hang off. Every field is optional and dropping any of them costs a nicer picture and nothing else.

rack_order.description: Left-to-right order of modules in the rack view. Ids not in the patch are ignored, and nodes missing from the list are appended, so an out-of-date list degrades rather than breaks.

controls.description: Performance surface. Deliberately separate from the DSP graph: the same parameter may be driven by a Godot knob, a browser slider, a DAW automation lane, a MIDI CC or a physical encoder without changing the graph.

automation.description: Recorded or authored parameter movement. Graph data, never hidden frontend state.

sequence.description: An optional looped step sequence, played by the editor through the same note path as the on-screen keys. A runtime that only wants to make sound may ignore it entirely; dropping it costs the tune and nothing else.

step.description: Which step the note starts on, from zero.

length.description: How many steps the note holds for.

presets.description: Named snapshots of the performance surface: the sound bank. A preset stores values by control id, never by node, so the graph can be rearranged without breaking the bank. Structure lives in nodes and connections; character lives here. The lesson of every patcher without this key is that it cannot be an afterthought.

node_id.description: Stable identity. Must survive rename, move, and re-serialization; connections and automation refer to it.

signal_type.description: audio and control are sample streams and interconvert freely. event and note are discrete messages and require an exact match.

type.description: Registry node type name, e.g. SawOscillator. Unknown types are a validation error, never a silent no-op.

name.description: Human-facing label. Purely cosmetic; never used for identity.

parameters.description: Parameter values by name. Omitted parameters take the registry default, so a minimal patch stays readable.

position.description: Editor layout hint. Runtimes ignore it; it lives here so a patch opens the same way in every editor.

module.description: When type is "module": the name of the definition this node instantiates. The instance exposes only the module's declared inputs, outputs and parameters.

host.description: Only on a seam — a node of type "Input" or "Output". Names the side of the machine this edge meets: "note" or "audio" for an input, "stereo" for an output. A seam inside a module must not carry one, because a module's seams are its ports and binding one to the machine would mean every instance shared that one keyboard. A seam at the top level may or may not: with a host it is where the graph meets its machine, and becomes the matching terminal node when the patch is loaded; without one it is a socket nothing is currently plugged into, and is spliced out at load, so whatever it fed goes silent. Nothing downstream of the loader learns the word either way.

to.description: Destination: an input port. An input accepts at most one connection unless the node type declares the port summing.

waypoint.description: Editor layout hint: a point the cable is routed through, set by dragging it. Like node positions, runtimes ignore it and it lives here so a patch looks the same in every editor.

group.description: Panel grouping. Controls sharing a group are drawn as one block on the performance surface, whatever nodes they target â€” an operator's own knobs and the gain node that sets its level belong together on the panel even though they are separate nodes in the graph. Absent means the control groups with others targeting the same node. Panel organization, never graph semantics.

target.description: The graph parameter this surface drives.

binding.description: Optional physical or protocol binding. Absent means the surface is on-screen only.

module.description: A named subgraph with a declared surface. Instances are expanded into plain nodes at load; a module is notation, not a runtime object. Definitions may not instantiate modules (no nesting). See docs/modules-design.md.

presets.description: The definition's sound bank, keyed by its controls' ids. Travels with the face when a patch becomes a device.

module_panel.description: The face an instance wears. Presentation only, like arrangement: it never changes what a patch sounds like and never changes the declared surface. An exported parameter left off the panel is still exported, still settable per instance, and still a legal control or automation target — it simply has no knob. Omit the whole object to get every export in declared order.

rows.description: Exported parameter names, grouped into panel rows, left to right and top to bottom. A name this module does not export is ignored, so an out-of-date panel degrades rather than breaks. Unlike arrangement.rack_order, exports missing from the rows are NOT appended: leaving one out is the authoring act.

labels.description: What the panel calls an export, by exported name. Derived export names like "op1_gain" say where a knob goes; a caption says what it does.

values.description: Control id to the value its target takes.
